newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says legal abortion rate lowest in 20 years.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says legal abortion rate lowest in 20 years.

text.p: The rate at which American women obtain legal abortions has fallen to its lowest level in two decades, following an almost five percent decrease in abortions reported in 1994, federal health officials said on Friday.
The U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said the number of legal abortions among women aged 15 to 44 decreased to 21 per 1,000 in 1994, the lowest rate since 1976.

A total of 1,267,415 legal abortions were reported in 1994, down 4.7 percent from 1993. The number of abortions reported to the CDC has steadily declined since the beginning of the decade, the agency said.
"The number of abortions peaked in 1990. That was also the year of the highest number of live births in the country," CDC epidemiologist Lisa Koonin said.

There were 321 abortions for every 1,000 live births in 1994, the latest year for which figures were available. The number was lower than for any year since 1976. In 1993, there were 334 abortions for every 1,000 live births.
The CDC said the national abortion rate increased every year between 1972 and 1980, then remained stable between 1981 and 1993, varying between 22 and 24 per 1,000 women of reproductive age.

The CDC said the decline in reported abortions may reflect reduced access to abortion services and changes in attitudes about having an abortion. It could also mean there were fewer unintended pregnancies.

The decline may also have occurred because more women are becoming less fertile as the nation's population ages. Women over 35, the age associated with lowest fertility, accounted for 25 percent of women of reproductive age in 1980 and 35 percent in 1994. The proportion of women under 30, considered to have the highest fertility, fell from 58 percent in 1980 to 46 percent in 1994.

Women who obtained legal abortions in 1994 were usually under 25, white and unmarried. About one-fifth of them were 19 or younger. "The proportion of abortions among teens has remained stable," Koonin said.
About 54 percent of legal abortions were performed during the first 8 weeks of pregnancy, the CDC said. About 88 percent were performed during the first 12 weeks.
The CDC report made no attempt to estimate the number of illegal abortions that may have occurred during the same period.
